prior_ai_research.title: Earlier AI research pass over original records
prior_ai_research.note: Compiled by an AI assistant working from census, vital and newspaper records, including record images. sams_death_cert_1913.title: Death certificate, Harriet Eliza Sams, 1913
sams_death_cert_1913.note: Image read here. Washington Co., Holston district; registration district 953, file no. 15-2409. Mrs. Harriet Eliza Lewis, white, married, housewife; born 4 August 1856 in Sullivan County, Tennessee; died 4 January 1913 aged 56 years 5 months 0 days. Father Hiram Samms, mother Jane Carrol, both birthplaces "Not Known". Cause tuberculosis of the trachea, duration unknown; attended 2 October to 19 December 1912. Informant Geo Lewis of Glade Spring, her husband. Buried Friendship Cemetery, 5 January 1913. Filed 7 January 1913.

lewis_obit_1955.title: Obituary, James H. Lewis, York Daily Record, 18 Jul 1955, p. 26
lewis_obit_1955.note: Read and quoted by an AI research pass; the image has not been re-examined here. Gives his address as 540 West King Street, death at 6 p.m. Saturday at York Hospital, retirement from the York Naval Ordnance plant, nine surviving children and four siblings. Its stated age of 70 does not agree with a birth of 12 December 1885.

lewis_obit_1944_death.title: "George W. Lewis, Stewartstown, Dies," York Daily Record, 8 Jan 1944, p. 10
lewis_obit_1944_death.note: Image read here. "George W. Lewis died yesterday at 2:30 p. m. at the home of his son-in-law and daughter, Mr. and Mrs. Baldwin Barbra, this place. Death was caused by complication of diseases. He was 83 years of age." Surviving: three sons — James H. (Maryland Line), Walter A. (Knoxville, Tenn.) and Frank T. (Pylesville, Md.); three daughters — Mrs. James Wyingear and Mrs. Eli Freedman, both of Fawn Grove R. D., and Mrs. Baldwin Barbra, with whom he lived. "Yesterday" fixes the death at 7 January 1944.

lewis_obit_1944_burial.title: "George W. Lewis, Stewartstown, Buried," York Daily Record, 11 Jan 1944, p. 8
lewis_obit_1944_burial.note: Image read here. Services held at the W. Howard Webb Funeral home, Fawn Grove; Rev. A. E. Ackerman, pastor of Fawn Grove Methodist church, officiating; interment Fawn Grove cemetery. Pallbearers: Harry Hovis, Lewis Walker, William Barbra, George Barbra, Robert Wynigear and Donald Lewis. Flowerbearers: Ruth Freeman, Emma Freeman, Mabel Freeman, Mrs. Lewis Walker, Cathrine Kunkle and Gladys Wynigear. Gives the death as "Friday", which was 7 January 1944.

va_vital_index_1905.title: Virginia, Vital Records, 1853–1934 — index entry for the 1905 Lewis/Stovall marriage

Groom's parents given as G Wm and Harriott; bride's parents column reads "Maggie" and nothing more. H B Miller named as officiant or bondsman. delayed_birth_bettie_lewis_1949.title: Delayed Certificate of Birth, Bettie Jane Lewis, filed 1949
delayed_birth_bettie_lewis_1949.note: Image read here. Line 11, "Mother of Child, full maiden name," reads "Harriett Booher." A sworn, notarized statement by Mrs. Flora Mae Greever, who cites a family Bible "printed in the year 1872" examined directly by notary David A. Rouse. Mother's race recorded white.

bible_notes_lewis.title: Handwritten notes on an old Lewis family Bible
bible_notes_lewis.note: Loose pages photographed here, of unknown authorship and date, mixing transcription of a Bible said to date to 1872 with later family recollection. Some entries are second- or third-hand. Separate notes found among the papers of Colleen Hoffman (Lorene Lewis's daughter) indicate that George W. Lewis himself wrote several of the entries in the underlying Bible; which of the transcribed lines are his is not marked. Records "Harriet Boar was in Old Bible" and that "Harret Bohr" is the form seen "more often in outside records"; also carries the Ike Ingram / housemaid story and a "Cherokee or Creek" ancestry note. A separate summary page gives George Lewis's parents as "William W.S. (Samuel William)" and "Elizabeth" with the family arriving from Charleston, SC in 1865 — contradicted outright by census and marriage records. Treated as highly questionable throughout.

census_1880_booher.title: 1880 U.S. census, Kinderhook District, Washington Co., Virginia — Jacob H. Booher household
census_1880_booher.note: FamilySearch index consulted here. Head Jacob H. Booher, age 19; Jane Booher, step-mother, age 40, born Tennessee; Elizabeth Samms, age 16, born Tennessee. Jane fits Harriet's mother, remarried into a Booher family after Hiram Sams's desertion; Elizabeth is a younger Sams daughter (b. c.1863–64), not Harriet.

census_1880_ingram.title: 1880 U.S. census, Holston District, Washington Co., Virginia — I. H. Ingram household
census_1880_ingram.note: FamilySearch index consulted here. I. H. Ingram, merchant, born c.1852; household is a wife and two young daughters, no servants. Matches the initials, trade and locale of the "Ike Ingram" of the family's Bible notes, and he is buried at Friendship Cemetery as Harriet was — but no record places Harriet in his household.

census_1860_washington_lewis.title: 1860 U.S. census, Washington Co., Virginia — Philip Lewis household
census_1860_washington_lewis.note: Read in an earlier session. Places Philip Lewis's family in Washington County, Virginia, months before George's birth in December 1860 — so there was no arrival from South Carolina in 1865, as the family's Bible notes claim.
